text:
sam_support: Customer (AcmeWidgets) pinging — they're seeing 1500ms p95 and requests landing in us-west even though their app sets cookie=region=eu. They pasted curl + headers. 

sam_support: Repro steps from customer:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -H 'X-Region: ' \n  -b 'region=eu' \n  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
They say router chooses west. They want data residency guarantee.

lina_infra: noted. Do we still treat empty X-Region header as highest precedence? IIRC header > cookie. If header present but empty it may be parsed as legitimate value (empty string) and wins our precedence logic. :thinking_face: 

jorge_engine: Correct — router precedence is header -> query -> cookie -> default. We didn't normalize empty-string values in the precedence comparator. I can pull logs for the req id if they provide one.

sam_support: customer provided req id 8a3f-req-002 in their app logs. Also included our front-edge trace: ``[edge] req=8a3f route=choose(region='') -> fallback=west``.

jorge_engine: grabbing edge logs now. short dump:
```
ts=2026-03-16T14:12:03Z req=8a3f headers={"X-Region":"","Cookie":"region=eu;..."} decision=choose_region(header_value="", cookie_value="eu") chosen=west reason="header present but empty wins"
```
So it's exactly that.

lina_infra: immediate mitigation: add an edge rule to treat empty X-Region as absent. We can push a short-lived rule in the routing layer to ignore zero-length header values. I can deploy a config within 30m.

sam_support: please do. Customer is asking for a mitigation and also wants a long-term fix. Also they noted billing spikes because requests route cross-region and egress costs rose.

jorge_engine: Proposed permanent fix: change comparator to consider empty-string equivalent to missing. Patch in router: `if trim(header) == "" then treat as null` and re-run precedence. I'll open a PR and flag eng-runtime for review. Will also add unit test for header CSVs and whitespace-only values.

lina_infra: Edge config quick hack (nginx map snippet we can apply to the proxy) — map empty to unset:
```
map $http_x_region $x_region_normalized {
  ""     "";
  default $http_x_region;
}
proxy_set_header X-Region $x_region_normalized;
```
That will remove empty header before routing. I'll stage in canary for 5% traffic to affected customer region.

sam_support: customer workaround in meantime: either explicitly set header to `eu` (no empty value) or remove header entirely so cookie wins. Example curl to remove header:
```
# remove header entirely
curl -H 'X-Region;' -b 'region=eu' https://... 
# or set header explicitly
curl -H 'X-Region: eu' -b 'region=eu' https://...
```
I'll forward this to customer.

devops-bot: Ticket SUP-9421 created (priority=P2) for routing-normalization; assignees: jorge_engine, lina_infra. Links: https://support.redwood.example/t/SUP-9421

jorge_engine: will open PR after lunch and link here. ETA for permanent fix: 2 business days (tests + rollout).

lina_infra: can confirm canary patch deployed to edge pool A (5%) at 14:45 UTC. Monitoring latency and region select counts.

sam_support: thanks — I'll update customer with the canary and the curl workarounds and confirm once canary shows improvement.

devops-bot: Canary metrics: region_selects (before): west=78%, eu=22%. after: west=31%, eu=69% (canary sample).

sam_support: nice, passing to customer now. Follow-up: please add regression alert so future router changes don't reintroduce empty-header precedence.

jorge_engine: adding tests + a lint rule in infra-config to detect empty-header precedence changes.

sam_support: closing loop when PR merged + SUP-9421 resolved. :white_check_mark:
